title: Concealed undoing: f83r P4 as a completion promise defeated by private unweaving
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A whole 33-group paragraph is nominated for a narrative where visible work and hidden undoing act on the same object while others rely on a completion promise. Discovery changes what the observers know and forces completion. The conditional next act is not asserted to have occurred.

design.whole_content_draft: A woman gives the public completion of a particular cloth as a condition for marriage. She works by day but secretly undoes work at night, keeping completion delayed. A disclosure exposes the night work and she is compelled to finish. The episode therefore changes both an object and other agents’ knowledge; completion permits the promised next step but does not assert that a marriage actually happened.
coupled_claims: A public undertaking makes completion of this cloth a prerequisite for a later social act.
Visible daytime work is counteracted by concealed night work on the same cloth.
Disclosure exposes the concealed action; coerced continuation then completes the cloth.

semantic_consequence.physical_state: The same cloth has a partial/completed state and amount of work; weaving increases completed work and unraveling decreases it. No exact nightly quantity or equal daily increment is supplied.
semantic_consequence.knowledge_state: Observers see or accept progress while not knowing the night undoing; disclosure invalidates that belief. The world state and reported belief are separate.
semantic_consequence.interaction: Daytime work alone would support eventual completion under continued positive progress; the hidden reverse action can keep the prerequisite false. Exposing and stopping that action changes the completion path even though the material and public goal stay the same.
semantic_consequence.source_endpoint: The narrated episode states forced completion, not a completed marriage. The target model must keep a completed prerequisite distinct from execution of the promised sequel.
semantic_consequence.target_consequence: Every qokeey must concern undoing the same work done by qokeedy, and chedy must retain one completion condition across a stated promise and any later endpoint. The late .28/.29 oldy mentions must remain nighttime in the same narrative, not switch to a degree or quantity.

concrete_rivals: An honest technical instruction alternating two necessary weaving operations has no concealed reversal defeating a public completion promise.
A story about two different cloths can have work and unraveling simultaneously without delaying the same object’s completion.
An omniscient narrator’s assertion and a character’s reported promise differ; treating every clause as an executed fact wrongly predicts the later social act.
lexical_syntax_and_source_debts: No target woman, cloth, time expression, marriage, quoted speech, disclosure or compulsion has been identified. The seven whole-form meanings are guesses.
The source is the bounded Penelope weaving episode within Antinous’s hostile speech, not an entire Homeric book and not a technical weaving manual.
The model does not assert exact cancellation, an infinite loop, three target repetitions, or a numeral for the source’s three/four years.
Adjacent shckhedy shckhedy remains UNKNOWN; it is not turned into two units of work or a concealed clock.
The final narrative change needs an actual written discovery/compulsion clause; it is not inserted as a free singleton gloss.
No pre1450 copy or channel connecting this ancient story to the Voynich manuscript was newly collated; historical plausibility is a genre-level consideration only.
